title: A Former Athlete's Comprehensive Daily Routine for Skin Health: From Porridge to Microneedling
text:
An in-depth look at a day in the life of a former sprint hurdler focusing on gut-friendly foods, targeted nutrients, and consistent skincare to combat inflammation, support mitochondrial function, and maintain youthful skin. The regimen includes specific breakfast and lunch recipes, the importance of fermented foods, key supplements like Brazil nuts for selenium, and the non-negotiable use of sunscreen. It also covers fitness habits and professional treatments like microneedling, all aimed at achieving calmer, clearer, and more resilient skin through holistic strategies.
The article presents a detailed daily regimen focused on diet, exercise, and skincare, as shared by an individual with a history in sprint hurdling. The morning routine begins with a carefully crafted porridge designed to stabilize blood sugar and provide sustained energy, accommodating dairy and gluten intolerances.
The base consists of gluten-free oats and almond milk, enhanced with chia seeds for fiber, pea protein powder, pumpkin seeds for zinc (a mineral beneficial for skin repair and acne-prone skin), and berries rich in polyphenols. These antioxidants protect collagen and reduce inflammation. The meal is finished with almond butter and occasionally maple syrup.
The importance of fermented foods, like kimchi, is emphasized for diversifying the gut microbiome, which connects to skin health through the gut-skin axis; a balanced gut reduces systemic inflammation, leading to calmer, clearer skin. Lunch typically features miso salmon, sweet potato, and a salad. Salmon provides Omega-3 fatty acids to support the skin barrier and calm inflammation.
The salad includes leafy greens such as spinach, chickpeas for gut health, half an avocado packed with healthy fats and vitamins A, C, and E (antioxidants that protect collagen), and sweet potato, which is high in beta carotene-acting as internal retinol to aid skin cell turnover, pore clarity, and radiance. Green tea is consumed after meals to mitigate oxidative stress and maintain mitochondrial health in skin cells; these cellular powerhouses are crucial for collagen synthesis and repair, and their function declines with age.
Specific supplements and foods are highlighted: a daily Brazil nut for selenium, an essential component of the skin's antioxidant defenses against UV damage; kiwi fruit for vitamin C (vital for collagen maintenance and dermal thickness), fiber, and melatonin to aid sleep; and Parmesan as a satisfying snack high in protein and umami. The fitness routine includes weight training twice weekly and spin classes, drawing from a background in high-intensity sports.
Regarding skincare, collagen supplements are dismissed in favor of a protein-rich diet. Vitamin D is taken for bone health and longevity. Broad-spectrum sunscreen with UVA filters is used year-round to prevent cumulative damage that leads to fine lines, wrinkles, and sagging-sagging being particularly irreversible as elastin production diminishes after the twenties. The Flawless Vitamin C NAD+ Serum is applied daily to the face, neck, and hands.
Microneedling is favored as an in-office treatment for its ability to harness the skin's innate repair capabilities with minimal downtime. The advice is framed as personal testimony given to Antonia Lenon
